nodes.label: Banks Act Guidance Note 4/2014 — Internal Ratings-Based Approach Application Process
nodes.author: Prudential Authority
nodes.norm_label: banks act guidance note 4/2014 — internal ratings-based approach application process

nodes.label: IRB Application Pack Requirement & Overview: Banks intending to adopt the Internal Ratings-Based approach must submit a completed IRB application pack signed by the CEO and board chairperson.
nodes.norm_label: irb application pack requirement & overview: banks intending to adopt the internal ratings-based approach must submit a completed irb application pack signed by the ceo and board chairperson.

nodes.label: 18-Month Application Period: Banks should allow up to 18 months between submitting the IRB application pack and receiving approval or denial.
nodes.norm_label: 18-month application period: banks should allow up to 18 months between submitting the irb application pack and receiving approval or denial.

nodes.label: Parallel Reporting Run Requirement: All IRB applicant banks must undertake a minimum six-month parallel reporting run for affected portfolios during the 18-month application period.
nodes.norm_label: parallel reporting run requirement: all irb applicant banks must undertake a minimum six-month parallel reporting run for affected portfolios during the 18-month application period.

nodes.label: Two-Stage IRB Application Process: The IRB application process consists of a documentation submission stage followed by an on-site focused supervisory review by BSD.
nodes.norm_label: two-stage irb application process: the irb application process consists of a documentation submission stage followed by an on-site focused supervisory review by bsd.

nodes.label: Bank Readiness and Roll-Out Plan: Banks must demonstrate a state of readiness with a clear IRB roll-out plan covering material portfolios before applying for advanced approach approval.
nodes.norm_label: bank readiness and roll-out plan: banks must demonstrate a state of readiness with a clear irb roll-out plan covering material portfolios before applying for advanced approach approval.

nodes.label: Application Pack Compilation Guidance: Banks must provide concise responses in the application pack to enable BSD to scope its supervisory review of the IRB application.
nodes.norm_label: application pack compilation guidance: banks must provide concise responses in the application pack to enable bsd to scope its supervisory review of the irb application.

nodes.label: IRB Implementation Plan and Milestones: Applicants must provide an overview of the IRB implementation plan, key milestones, and internal or external expertise utilised.
nodes.norm_label: irb implementation plan and milestones: applicants must provide an overview of the irb implementation plan, key milestones, and internal or external expertise utilised.

nodes.label: Rationale for Adopting Advanced Approaches: Banks must summarise their reasons for applying for the advanced IRB approaches and the objectives they aim to achieve.
nodes.norm_label: rationale for adopting advanced approaches: banks must summarise their reasons for applying for the advanced irb approaches and the objectives they aim to achieve.

nodes.label: Group Structure and Scope of Application: Banks must detail group and legal entity structure and map the scope of the IRB application to relevant asset classes on form BA 200.
nodes.norm_label: group structure and scope of application: banks must detail group and legal entity structure and map the scope of the irb application to relevant asset classes on form ba 200.

nodes.label: Permanent Exemption Portfolios: Banks must detail any portfolios for which they seek permanent exemption from the advanced approaches.
nodes.norm_label: permanent exemption portfolios: banks must detail any portfolios for which they seek permanent exemption from the advanced approaches.

nodes.label: Corporate Governance and IRB Oversight: Banks must describe the governance framework for IRB implementation, including model development, maintenance, and independent validation.
nodes.norm_label: corporate governance and irb oversight: banks must describe the governance framework for irb implementation, including model development, maintenance, and independent validation.

nodes.label: Board-Approved Credit Policy: Banks must submit a copy of the board-approved credit policy and describe any planned future changes.
nodes.norm_label: board-approved credit policy: banks must submit a copy of the board-approved credit policy and describe any planned future changes.

nodes.label: Model Validation, Development and Monitoring Policies: Banks must submit board-approved policies covering model validation, development, and monitoring.
nodes.norm_label: model validation, development and monitoring policies: banks must submit board-approved policies covering model validation, development, and monitoring.

nodes.label: IRB Self-Assessment Schedules: Banks must complete and submit schedules 1, 2 and 3 of the IRB self-assessment templates published by the SARB.
nodes.norm_label: irb self-assessment schedules: banks must complete and submit schedules 1, 2 and 3 of the irb self-assessment templates published by the sarb.

nodes.label: Rating and Risk Estimation System Documentation: Banks must complete Annexure B for each model to be used under the IRB approach, including all relevant supporting documentation.
nodes.norm_label: rating and risk estimation system documentation: banks must complete annexure b for each model to be used under the irb approach, including all relevant supporting documentation.

nodes.label: Credit Risk Rating System Register: Banks must complete and submit a Credit Risk Rating System Register as specified by the SARB.
nodes.norm_label: credit risk rating system register: banks must complete and submit a credit risk rating system register as specified by the sarb.

nodes.label: South African Environment Model Tailoring: Banks must describe the process followed to tailor models to the South African environment and branch management's input into model development.
nodes.norm_label: south african environment model tailoring: banks must describe the process followed to tailor models to the south african environment and branch management's input into model development.

nodes.label: Rating System Experience Requirement: Banks must demonstrate they meet the experience requirement by detailing how long their rating and scoring systems have been in operation.
nodes.norm_label: rating system experience requirement: banks must demonstrate they meet the experience requirement by detailing how long their rating and scoring systems have been in operation.

nodes.label: Use Test Compliance: Banks must summarise compliance with the use test, showing how rating systems are integral to credit approval, risk reporting, and internal capital allocation.
nodes.norm_label: use test compliance: banks must summarise compliance with the use test, showing how rating systems are integral to credit approval, risk reporting, and internal capital allocation.

nodes.label: Regulatory vs Internal Parameter Estimates: Banks must outline any differences between parameter estimates used for regulatory capital purposes and those used internally.
nodes.norm_label: regulatory vs internal parameter estimates: banks must outline any differences between parameter estimates used for regulatory capital purposes and those used internally.

nodes.label: Credit Risk Stress Testing Approach: Banks must describe their credit risk stress testing approach and demonstrate compliance with regulation 23(11)(b)(ix).
nodes.norm_label: credit risk stress testing approach: banks must describe their credit risk stress testing approach and demonstrate compliance with regulation 23(11)(b)(ix).

nodes.label: Data Management and Technological Environment: Banks must describe their data management approach, including systems used for storing rating and parameter information, with reference to regulation 23(11)(b)(viii).
nodes.norm_label: data management and technological environment: banks must describe their data management approach, including systems used for storing rating and parameter information, with reference to regulation 23(11)(b)(viii).

nodes.label: Calibration Databases and Regulatory Reporting: Banks must describe how calibration databases and regulatory capital figures are obtained and confirm ability to submit risk-based returns within prescribed periods.
nodes.norm_label: calibration databases and regulatory reporting: banks must describe how calibration databases and regulatory capital figures are obtained and confirm ability to submit risk-based returns within prescribed periods.

nodes.label: Independent Validation Approach: Banks must describe their validation approach covering back-testing, performance monitoring, and benchmarking of rating system parameter estimates.
nodes.norm_label: independent validation approach: banks must describe their validation approach covering back-testing, performance monitoring, and benchmarking of rating system parameter estimates.

nodes.label: Validation Unit Staffing: Banks must detail the staffing of their validation unit, including approved vacancies and required skillsets.
nodes.norm_label: validation unit staffing: banks must detail the staffing of their validation unit, including approved vacancies and required skillsets.

nodes.label: Annexure B — Rating System Detail Template: Annexure B requires banks to provide structured details for each rating system including methodology, weaknesses, portfolio coverage, and approval committee information.
nodes.norm_label: annexure b — rating system detail template: annexure b requires banks to provide structured details for each rating system including methodology, weaknesses, portfolio coverage, and approval committee information.

nodes.label: Parameter Estimates and Capital Information Table: Banks must complete a table providing exposure, EAD, PD, and LGD data as at a specified date for each rating system submitted in Annexure B.
nodes.norm_label: parameter estimates and capital information table: banks must complete a table providing exposure, ead, pd, and lgd data as at a specified date for each rating system submitted in annexure b.

nodes.label: Banks Act Guidance Note 2/2025 — Internal Ratings-Based Approach for Credit Risk
nodes.author: Prudential Authority
nodes.norm_label: banks act guidance note 2/2025 — internal ratings-based approach for credit risk

nodes.label: GN 2/2025 (IRB Credit Risk) — Introduction: Introduces the guidance note arising from a 2021 PA discussion paper on IRB credit risk model requirements, directed at IRB-approved banks.
nodes.norm_label: gn 2/2025 (irb credit risk) — introduction: introduces the guidance note arising from a 2021 pa discussion paper on irb credit risk model requirements, directed at irb-approved banks.

nodes.label: GN 2/2025 (IRB Credit Risk) — Guidance related to specified matters: Provides IRB-specific guidance on CRM capital treatment, local government/PSE exposure taxonomy, and rating assignment horizon for IRB-approved banks.
nodes.norm_label: gn 2/2025 (irb credit risk) — guidance related to specified matters: provides irb-specific guidance on crm capital treatment, local government/pse exposure taxonomy, and rating assignment horizon for irb-approved banks.

nodes.label: GN 2/2025 (IRB Credit Risk) — Acknowledgement of receipt: Requires all recipient institutions to provide a signed acknowledgement of receipt from the CEO and independent auditors to the PA.
nodes.norm_label: gn 2/2025 (irb credit risk) — acknowledgement of receipt: requires all recipient institutions to provide a signed acknowledgement of receipt from the ceo and independent auditors to the pa.

nodes.label: Banks Act Guidance Note 9/2022 — Credit Risk Models (IRB Approach)
nodes.author: Prudential Authority
nodes.norm_label: banks act guidance note 9/2022 — credit risk models (irb approach)

nodes.label: Introduction: This guidance note addresses IRB credit risk model requirements for banks approved to use the Internal Ratings-Based approach, which does not apply to this bank using the standardised approach.
nodes.norm_label: introduction: this guidance note addresses irb credit risk model requirements for banks approved to use the internal ratings-based approach, which does not apply to this bank using the standardised approach.

nodes.label: Model documentation quality: Requirements for IRB banks to maintain high-quality model development and validation documentation are specific to IRB-approved institutions, not this bank.
nodes.norm_label: model documentation quality: requirements for irb banks to maintain high-quality model development and validation documentation are specific to irb-approved institutions, not this bank.

nodes.label: LGD estimates for defaulted loans: Regulatory requirements for estimating LGDs on defaulted loans under the IRB framework are not applicable to a standardised-approach bank.
nodes.norm_label: lgd estimates for defaulted loans: regulatory requirements for estimating lgds on defaulted loans under the irb framework are not applicable to a standardised-approach bank.

nodes.label: LGD overrides: Guidance on LGD override processes for capital calculations is exclusively relevant to IRB-approved banks and does not apply to this institution.
nodes.norm_label: lgd overrides: guidance on lgd override processes for capital calculations is exclusively relevant to irb-approved banks and does not apply to this institution.

nodes.label: Quality and representativeness of development datasets: Requirements for development datasets used in IRB credit risk models, including low-default portfolios, are not relevant to a non-IRB bank.
nodes.norm_label: quality and representativeness of development datasets: requirements for development datasets used in irb credit risk models, including low-default portfolios, are not relevant to a non-irb bank.

nodes.label: The definition and incorporation of downturn in LGDs and EADs: IRB-specific obligations to incorporate economic downturn conditions into LGD and EAD estimates do not apply to this standardised-approach institution.
nodes.norm_label: the definition and incorporation of downturn in lgds and eads: irb-specific obligations to incorporate economic downturn conditions into lgd and ead estimates do not apply to this standardised-approach institution.

nodes.label: The treatment of stale ratings: Requirements for IRB banks to regularly refresh internal ratings to reflect current credit risk are not applicable to this bank's standardised-approach framework.
nodes.norm_label: the treatment of stale ratings: requirements for irb banks to regularly refresh internal ratings to reflect current credit risk are not applicable to this bank's standardised-approach framework.

nodes.label: Validation: Annual independent validation requirements for IRB credit risk models used in RWA calculations are specific to IRB-approved banks and do not bind this institution.
nodes.norm_label: validation: annual independent validation requirements for irb credit risk models used in rwa calculations are specific to irb-approved banks and do not bind this institution.

nodes.label: Acknowledgement of receipt: Purely procedural requirement for IRB banks to return a signed acknowledgement to the PA and share the guidance note with auditors, not applicable to this institution.
nodes.norm_label: acknowledgement of receipt: purely procedural requirement for irb banks to return a signed acknowledgement to the pa and share the guidance note with auditors, not applicable to this institution.

nodes.label: Banks Act Guidance Note 3/2014 — Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: Introduction: Introduces the BCBS Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (January 2013) aimed at strengthening risk management practices across banks.
Objective of the Questionnaire: Requires all banks to complete a questionnaire to assess readiness to comply with the BCBS Principles by 1 January 2017 as part of a coordinated monitoring approach.
Introduction (duplicate): Reiterates the background and purpose of the BCBS Principles for risk data aggregation and reporting as the basis for this guidance note.
Objective of the Questionnaire (duplicate): Reiterates the requirement for banks to complete the group-level questionnaire to demonstrate progress toward compliance with the Principles.
Participating Banks: Mandates that all South African banks and branches of foreign institutions must complete the questionnaire, directly binding this bank.

Completing the Questionnaire: Requires each participating bank to designate a sufficiently senior key contact person to liaise with the Prudential Authority for the purposes of the questionnaire exercise.
Banks Act Guidance Note 3/2016 — Credit Risk and Accounting for Expected Credit Losses
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: GN 3/2016 — BCBS Guidance on Credit Risk and Accounting for Expected Credit Losses: Introduces BCBS supervisory guidance on sound credit risk practices for expected credit loss accounting frameworks, relevant sector-wide but indirectly applicable to an institutional-only bank with limited credit-exposure-generating activities.
Background — BCBS December 2015 Document: References the BCBS December 2015 guidance document on credit risk and ECL accounting as the source material underpinning this guidance note.

Scope of BCBS Guidance: Establishes that the BCBS guidance covers supervisory expectations for the implementation and ongoing application of ECL accounting frameworks, applicable broadly across the banking sector.
Banks Act Guidance Note 5/2016 — Corporate Governance Principles for Banks
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: Background: Section 60B of the Banks Act and regulation 39 impose a direct statutory duty on this bank's board and executive officers to establish and maintain adequate and effective corporate governance processes commensurate with the bank's nature, complexity and risks.

Documents issued by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision relating to corporate governance principles for banks: The BCBS July 2015 corporate governance guidelines inform the principles and guidance that the Prudential Authority expects banks to apply, making them a key reference for this bank's governance framework design and ongoing compliance.

Acknowledgement of receipt: A procedural requirement obliging the bank's CEO and independent auditors to sign and return an acknowledgement of receipt of this guidance note to the Prudential Authority.
Banks Act Guidance Note 7/2016 — Capital Arbitrage Transactions
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: GN 7/2016 (Capital Arbitrage) — Section 1: Describes strategies used in capital arbitrage transactions designed to offset regulatory capital adjustments, including securities issuance, sales contracts, and collateralised derivatives, which are relevant to this bank's OTC derivative and structured activities.

GN 7/2016 (Capital Arbitrage) — Section 2: Continues enumeration of capital arbitrage strategies (including guarantees) that the Prudential Authority scrutinises, relevant to ensuring this bank's OTC derivative and capital structure transactions do not constitute impermissible regulatory capital offsets.
Banks Act Guidance Note 9/2008 — Stress Testing
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: GN 9/2008 (Stress Testing) — Some selected excerpts: Sets out IRB-approach credit risk stress testing requirements under Pillar 1 Regulation 23(11)(b)(ix), which are binding only on banks that have adopted the IRB approach for credit risk measurement.

GN 9/2008 (Stress Testing) — The process for submission: Describes submission processes for Pillar 2 stress tests via ICAAP and Pillar 1 IRB credit risk stress test results during on-site reviews, applicable to banks using the IRB approach rather than standardised credit risk measurement.
Banks Act Guidance Note 5/2022 — Effective Implementation of Group Controls (AML/CFT)
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: Introduction: Establishes FATF Recommendation 18 as the basis requiring financial groups to implement group-wide AML/CFT programmes including intra-group information sharing policies.

The implementation of AML/CFT group controls in banks' and controlling companies' foreign operations: Requires foreign operations of South African banking groups to declare compliance with local AML/CFT legislation via Form BA 099A, relevant if this bank is part of a group with foreign operations.

Ensuring effective implementation of group controls: Requires adequate skills, resources, and assurance mechanisms (audit and compliance) to effectively implement AML/CFT group controls across the group.
Terminology: Defines key AML/CFT terms including Recommendation 18, customer due diligence, and enhanced due diligence for consistent application across the guidance note.
Acknowledgement of receipt: Requires the CEO and independent auditors to sign and return an acknowledgement of receipt of this guidance note to the Prudential Authority.
Banks Act Guidance Note 10/2022 — Supervisory Guidelines: Prevention of Unlawful Activities
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: Introduction: Establishes the FATF risk-based approach requirement for ML/TF/PF risk assessment, which is directly binding on this bank as a SARB-licensed institution subject to AML/CFT obligations.

Definitions: Defines Crypto Assets and Crypto Asset Service Providers relevant to scoping AML/CFT obligations, material if the bank has any indirect exposure to CASPs through institutional counterparties.

Application of a risk-based approach: Identification and assessment of risks relative to CAs and CASPs: Requires banks to assess direct and indirect ML/TF/PF exposure to CAs and CASPs, relevant to the extent this bank's institutional counterparties engage in crypto-related activities.

Monitoring of client relationships: Directly requires ongoing transaction monitoring of client activity and reporting of suspicious or unusual activity to the FIC, binding on this bank in respect of all its institutional counterparties.

Acknowledgment of receipt: Requires the CEO to sign and return an acknowledgment of receipt to the PA and to provide a copy to the institution's independent auditors, a procedural compliance obligation directly applicable to this bank.
Banks Act Guidance Note 3/2025 — Climate-Related Disclosures for Banks
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: GN 3/2025 (Climate Disclosures) — Introduction: All SARB-licensed banks must build capacity to identify, assess, manage and disclose climate-related risks and opportunities as a matter of safety and soundness.
Principles and conceptual foundations for disclosures: Sets out the core principles and conceptual foundations that banks must apply when preparing climate-related disclosures.

Supervisory expectations: Banks are required to produce high-quality, decision-useful climate-related disclosure reports meeting both the stated principles and PA supervisory expectations across qualitative and quantitative dimensions.

Governance: Banks must disclose board and management governance structures, processes and controls for oversight of climate-related risks and opportunities including impacts on business model and strategy.

Strategy: Banks must disclose current and anticipated effects of material climate-related risks and opportunities on their business model, value chain and financial planning across relevant time horizons.
Risk management: Banks must disclose the processes and policies used to identify, assess, prioritise, monitor and integrate climate-related risks into their overall risk management framework.
Transition risk methodology: Banks must disclose the methodology, sector criteria, time horizons and scenario approaches used to determine which exposures are subject to material transition risk.

Physical risk methodology: Banks must disclose the methodology and selected material climate-related chronic and acute physical events used to assess which exposures are subject to material physical risk.

Concentration risk disclosures: Banks must disclose the potential effects of concentrated exposures to counterparties facing material transition or physical risks and the processes used to identify and assess such vulnerabilities.

Quantitative disclosure templates (BCBS Annexure 1): Banks must complete and publish BCBS-prescribed quantitative templates covering transition-risk exposures and financed emissions by sector as well as physical-risk exposure data.

Additional considerations: Where relevant, disclosures should incorporate South Africa-specific transition pathways and, for environmentally sustainable financing targets, reference the South African green finance taxonomy.

Assurance requirements: External assurance is not currently mandated but banks must subject climate disclosures to internal governance and controls equivalent to those used for financial reporting, with external assurance expected in future.
Implementation: The PA expects proactive, non-compliance-driven implementation of climate risk management and disclosures, with proportionate application and continuous improvement over time.
Acknowledgement of receipt: Banks must provide a copy of this Guidance Note to their independent auditors and return a signed acknowledgement of receipt from the CEO and auditors to the PA.
Banks Act Guidance Note 3/2010 — Market Risk Hypothetical Back-Testing (IMA Banks)
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: GN 3/2010 Section 2 — Hypothetical Back-Testing Reporting Requirements (BA320/BA325): IMA-approved banks must report hypothetical back-testing exceptions on monthly form BA320 (lines 96–106, column 6) and daily form BA325 (lines 20–30, column 3/5).

GN 3/2010 Section 3 — Basel Committee Further Guidelines on VaR Model Justification: Basel consultative guidance (January 2009) requires IMA banks to justify any significant changes to their internal VaR models, informing future regulatory expectations for model governance.

GN 3/2010 Section 4 — Hypothetical Back-Testing Process and Terminology: Prescribes the detailed process and terminology for hypothetical back-testing, mapping portfolio and desk-level exceptions to specific BA320 and BA325 line items.

GN 3/2010 Section 5 — Ex-Post Hypothetical P&L vs Ex-Ante VaR Comparison Methodology: Defines how the ex-post hypothetical daily P&L (static T-1 portfolio revalued at T prices) must be compared against the ex-ante VaR to determine back-testing exceptions, noting there is currently no separate standalone regulatory obligation beyond this comparison.
Banks Act Guidance Note 6/2022 — Business Risk Assessments (AML/CFT)
nodes.author: Prudential Authority

nodes.label: Introduction: Establishes that all banks must conduct a business-level ML/TF/PF risk assessment as the foundation of their risk-based AML/CFT approach, directly binding on this SARB-licensed bank.

Identification of ML/TF/PF risk: Requires banks to identify ML/TF/PF risks using national risk assessments, regulatory frameworks, and institution-specific data sources, directly applicable to this bank given its OTC derivatives, FX spot, and bond/equity activities.

Assessing ML/TF/PF risk: Requires banks to assess the likelihood and impact of identified ML/TF/PF threats on the institution and sector, directly binding and relevant to this bank's institutional counterparty profile and product mix.

Trigger Events: Mandates banks to review their risk assessments upon defined trigger events such as new products, new markets, or regulatory changes, directly binding on this bank particularly given potential expansion of trading activities.

Risk factor consideration examples: Provides illustrative risk factors banks must consider in their business risk assessments, directly relevant to this bank's customer base, geographic exposure, products, and delivery channels.
References: Lists reference sources consulted in drafting the guidance note; purely procedural with no binding obligation.

Terminology: Defines key terms including DPIP, FPPO, and FATF Recommendations used throughout the guidance note; relevant sector-wide but primarily operative where the bank onboards PEP-related counterparties.

Acknowledgement of receipt: Requires the CEO and independent auditors to sign and return an acknowledgement of receipt of this guidance note to the Prudential Authority, a direct administrative obligation on this bank.
